target_customer: Small and mid sized businesses, schools and teams that need to text customers and staff and later a mobile business phone system
problem: Businesses and organizations needed to message groups of people by SMS without personal phone numbers and with replies, scheduling and shared inboxes.
business_model: Freemium SaaS subscription with premium plans; later business phone system plans
product_category: Business SMS and cloud phone system

founders.name: Garrett Johnson
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (April 2012) says he first wanted a communication system for his nephew's school in Tampa. Education and prior employers not given.

founders.name: Ash Rust
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder and quoted by TechCrunch. No background found.

competitors.name: GroupMe
competitors.what: Group messaging by SMS and app, raised in a 2012 Hacker News comparison thread

competitors.name: Google Voice
competitors.what: Free calling, texting and voicemail, the comparison TechCrunch used when SendHub added calls in June 2012

technical_complexity.rationale: Built on Twilio's SMS and voice APIs, so the carrier layer was outsourced. The work was product and scheduling on top of an API.

defensibility.rationale: Built on a commodity API with many similar SMS tools; stickiness came from customer contact lists and group setups.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent acquired it; Cameo Global, a cloud telecom firm, bought it in June 2016.

market_need_then: TechCrunch reported 62,000 dollars of revenue in the first month of the premium plan and about 40 percent weekly self serve revenue growth in April 2012, with a message volume jump from 30,000 per month to 30,000 per week between February and March 2012.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and simple, tagline Simple Business SMS

branding.community_and_virality: No source found on community or merch. Press coverage was about growth and funding rather than the brand.

brand_strength.rationale: No evidence of a distinctive brand asset; coverage centered on growth numbers and the name is a descriptive compound.

pivots.to: Messaging plus calls and voicemail, then a mobile business phone system
pivots.why: Expanded to compete with Google Voice, later positioned as a mobile alternative to business phone systems (TechCrunch 2012 and 2013).

outcome_analysis: SendHub grew quickly after YC, with early premium revenue reported by TechCrunch in 2012, then raised a 2 million seed, 3 million Series A and 5 million Series B totalling about 10 million. It was acquired in June 2016 by Cameo Global at an undisclosed price; the CEO said several corporations had shown interest over the years. The product remains live and the site footer now names New Era Technology as owner.
notes: Dates conflict: CB Insights lists Series B as February 2014, PRWeb says November 19 2014; used the company release. Total raised about 10M per the release. Founder names come from TechCrunch, the YC page lists none. Site footer in 2026 says a New Era Technology company, a later ownership change not researched. Exit date from the June 2016 release.
